info.title: LuraDB API
info.description: REST-native multi-model database — KeyValue and JSON engines. `version` is the API contract version (see API_VERSION), independent of the server version; the latter is in the `x-luradb-server-version` extension. Runtime check: GET /version.

get.summary: `GET /health` — public heartbeat endpoint.
get.description: Returns a JSON snapshot of system vitals. No authentication required.

get.summary:
Returns all created users (admins and regular users) with their domain
permission matrix. API keys are not included.
get.description:
For `role == "Admin"`, `permissions` is meaningless for access control:
admins have unconditional access regardless of its contents (kv/012). It
is usually empty for an admin but not guaranteed to be — e.g. a user
promoted to admin via `luradb.toml` keeps any permissions set before the
promotion. Never read an empty array as "no access" or a non-empty one as
a restriction on an Admin row.

The list reflects the permission table as stored — it is not cross-checked
against existing domains, so an entry for a since-deleted (or not-yet-created)
domain is shown unchanged.

200.description: List of all users (without API keys), including their domain permissions

post.summary:
Creates a new user with the `User` role.
The API key is returned **only in this response** and is not stored afterward.
Only admins may call this endpoint.

201.description: User created. API key is shown once in the response.

delete.summary:
Deletes a user and all of their domain permissions.
The user's API key becomes invalid immediately — in-flight requests with the old key then get `401`.

post.summary:
Sets or overwrites a user's access permission on a domain.
`access` must be `"read"`, `"write"`, or `"ddl"` — each level includes the
lower ones. For `kv` the domain must exist; `json`/`rel` only check the name.

delete.summary:
Revokes a user's access permission on a specific domain.
`?store_type=json`/`rel` revokes a JSON/rel domain permission (default: kv).
After this call, the user's requests to this domain get `403 Forbidden`.

post.summary:
Generates a new API key for the user and immediately invalidates the old one.
The new key is returned **only in this response**.
Use this after key leaks or for regular key rotation.

get.summary:
Returns the caller's own identity. Unlike every other endpoint under this
tag, reachable by any authenticated caller — not admin-only (the
`auth_layer` middleware whitelists this path, see `middleware.rs`).
get.description:
Checked in order: `auth.enabled = false` → `Disabled`; a `TrustedPeer`
(UDS peer authenticated by the kernel, spec perf/001) → `TrustedPeer`;
otherwise the Bearer key is resolved to its `UserRecord` → `Admin`/`User`.
A `401` past the `auth_layer` middleware (which already validates the key)
can only mean a middleware bug — fail-closed, analogous to `enforce_sql_level`.

200.description: Caller identity — name (if any) and role

get.summary:
Lists every backup archive in `backup.dir`, plus the currently running
backup job (if any) separately in `running`.

post.summary: Starts an on-demand backup job (spec general/006 scope syntax for `scope`).

409.description: A backup or restore job is already running

503.description: Backup is disabled, or scope requires the JSON engine, which is disabled

post.summary:
Streams the request body to `backup.dir`, verifies its checksum and
manifest, then assigns it a fresh server-side id (`bk_..._upload[_N]`) —
the id in the manifest is never adopted. Invalid archives are discarded.

requestBody.description: NDJSON backup archive, raw bytes streamed to disk (no multipart)

400.description: Invalid backup file — checksum/manifest verification failed

get.summary:
Manifest fields + state + size for one backup. A backup whose job is
still running (no `.ndjson` file yet, only `.part`) reports `state:
"running"` from the in-RAM job slot instead of 404.

delete.summary:
Deletes a backup archive file. Refuses while the id is the currently
running job (or a stale `.part` leftover still exists for it).

409.description: The backup job for this id is still running

get.summary:
Streams the archive (`ServeFile`/tower-http `fs`) with HTTP Range support
for resumable downloads (spec general/006).

409.description: The backup job for this id is still running

post.summary:
Starts a restore job from an existing backup archive. The single-domain
remap and format-version checks happen synchronously here; a domain
already existing (`fail_if_exists`) only surfaces asynchronously via
`GET /restores/{id}`.

400.description: Invalid id/mode, remap requires a single domain, unsupported format version, or invalid backup file

404.description: Backup not found, or scope targets a missing domain

409.description: A backup or restore job is already running

get.summary: `GET /config` — effective configuration of the running process. Admin only.
get.description:
The path carries no `{domain}` segment, so `extract_domain` returns `None`
and the auth layer's None-branch requires an admin role (spec
general/022). The admin API key never appears in the body — redaction
happens at the field level (`AdminEntry.api_key`'s `#[serde(skip_serializing)]`
in config.rs), not in this handler.

200.description: config_path (resolved path, always set), config_file_loaded (whether a file existed there), and config (the effective LuraConfig — see config.rs for field docs)

get.summary: Returns all active domains with their names and creation timestamps.

post.summary:
Creates a new logical domain (isolated KV namespace).
Domain names must be unique, max 50 chars, and match `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]`.

get.summary: Returns metadata for a single domain by name. Returns 404 if it does not exist.

delete.summary:
Schedules a domain and all its data for deletion.
The domain becomes immediately inaccessible; the actual purge runs in the background.

get.summary:
Opens a Server-Sent Events stream of global lifecycle/DDL events: domains created, deleted and
purged across all three engines, plus relational table/view/index DDL and JSON index DDL.
Admin-only — the path carries no domain segment, so the standard auth middleware rejects any
non-admin caller (spec general/018 §3).
get.description:
A `Last-Event-ID` (header or `?last_event_id=`, header wins) resumes gaplessly from an in-memory
replay ring when possible; otherwise the server emits `event: reset` before continuing live. This
stream has its own tag (`g`) and sequence, entirely independent of `GET /store-api/kv/{domain}/watch`'s
(`w`) — an id from one stream is `unknown_id` at the other.

parameters.name: last_event_id
parameters.description: Resume id from a previous `id:` (or `event: reset`) — for callers that cannot set headers. Ignored when the `Last-Event-ID` header is present.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Resume id from a previous `id:` (or `event: reset`); set automatically by a native `EventSource`'s auto-reconnect. Takes precedence over `?last_event_id=`.

200.description: SSE stream of lifecycle/DDL events across the KV, JSON and relational engines: domains created/deleted/purged, and (rel) table/view/index DDL, (json) index DDL. No per-key data events — use a domain's `watch` for those. Every event carries an `id:`; `event:` matches its `type` field (e.g. `domain_created`, `table_altered`). `data:` is JSON `{engine, type, domain, object?, ts}` — `object` is the table/view/index/field name, absent for domain events. `event: reset` (`data: {"reason": ...}`) is emitted whenever gapless resume cannot be guaranteed.

403.description: Non-admin caller — this endpoint has no `{domain}` segment, so it is admin-only

get.summary: Returns all active JSON domains.

post.summary: Creates a new JSON domain (isolated document namespace, separate from KV domains).

get.summary:
Returns metadata for a single JSON domain, including its document count.
Domains in `deleting` state answer with 410 Gone.

410.description: Domain is being deleted (background purge running)

delete.summary: Marks a JSON domain as deleting. Documents become inaccessible immediately.

post.summary: Imports documents from an NDJSON body in atomic batches.

requestBody.description: NDJSON — one document per line, optional _key field

get.summary: Lists documents of a domain without filters (natural key order).

post.summary: Stores a document under a system-generated UUIDv4 key (create-only).

201.description: Document created with generated UUIDv4 key

get.summary: Counts all documents of a domain (key scan only).

Reads a document; `_key`/`_version` are top-level fields and an opaque
`ETag` is exposed for use with `If-Match` (json/011).

put.summary:
Upserts a document. With an `If-Match: "<etag>"` header the write is a
conditional update that fails with 409 on a version mismatch. With
`If-None-Match: *` the write is create-only and fails with 412 if the
document already exists (json/014); the two headers are mutually
exclusive (400).

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Only `*` is supported: create-only write, 412 if the document exists

400.description: Invalid key, invalid If-Match or If-None-Match header, or both headers set together

404.description: Domain not found, or If-Match on missing document

delete.summary:
Deletes a document and its index entries. Supports conditional delete via
`If-Match: "<etag>"`.

get.summary: Streams all documents of a domain as NDJSON without full buffering.
Lists all index definitions of a domain.

post.summary:
Creates an index definition. Existing documents are NOT back-indexed —
trigger a re-index for that.
Starts a background re-index of the domain (all indexes, or one field).

409.description: Re-index already running for this domain

get.summary:
Returns the status of a re-index task. Tasks are domain-scoped: a task id
of another domain answers 404 (tenant isolation).

404.description: Unknown task id for this domain

post.summary:
Searches documents via indexed fields. Filters: `"field": value` for
equality or `"field": {"$gt": …}` for ranges; multiple fields are ANDed.

get.summary:
Counts live keys in the domain, optionally filtered by a prefix — the same
semantics as `GET …/keys?prefix=`, without transferring the keys themselves.

200.description: Number of live keys matching the prefix. A full key scan under the hood (same cost as the equivalent `keys?prefix=` call) — cost grows linearly with domain size, so this is meant for on-demand use, not high-frequency polling.

get.summary: Lists all keys in the domain, optionally filtered by a prefix. Returns an empty array if no keys match.

delete.summary:
Deletes every live key whose raw form starts with `prefix`, optionally narrowed by a case-sensitive
`contains` substring filter on the key — the same selection `GET …/keys?prefix=&contains=` would show.
Atomic: either every matched key is gone, or (a 413) none is. Returns the number of keys deleted.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Key prefix — required, must not be empty. A domain-emptying request needs the admin-only DELETE /store-api/domains/{name} instead.

parameters.name: contains
parameters.description: Case-sensitive substring filter on the user key, applied to the prefix scan's results before the cap check

200.description: Matched keys deleted atomically (one write batch); an empty selection is a no-op

413.description: The selection exceeds max_bulk_delete_keys; no key was deleted

get.summary:
Retrieves the raw byte value for a key. Returns 204 for a key in the null state and 404 if the key does not exist or has expired.
When the key has a TTL, the response carries an `X-Expires-At` header with the absolute Unix-seconds expiry.

200.description: Value (raw bytes; an empty value yields an empty body). The `X-Expires-At` header (absolute Unix seconds) is present only when the key has a TTL.

204.description: Key exists in the explicit null state (set via PATCH …/null)

put.summary:
Inserts or updates a value for the given key (upsert semantics).
The optional `ttl` query parameter sets an expiry in seconds; omitting it stores the key indefinitely.

delete.summary: Permanently removes a key from the domain. The operation is idempotent; deleting a non-existent key still returns 204.

get.summary:
Returns a key's TTL expiry and last-modified time without reading its value (no VLog dereference).
`last_modified_at` is the write time of the newest visible version (PUT, or PATCH …/null) — not a
creation timestamp; every overwrite advances it.

patch.summary:
Sets the key to an explicit null value (upsert): the key stays registered and appears in scans,
but carries no data — GET answers 204. A write like any other; it resets a previously set TTL.

200.description: Key set to the null value state

get.summary:
Opens a Server-Sent Events stream that delivers real-time change events (`set` / `delete`) for keys matching the optional prefix.
The connection stays open until the client disconnects; a keep-alive ping is sent automatically.
get.description:
A `Last-Event-ID` (header or `?last_event_id=`, spec kv/024) resumes gaplessly from an in-memory
replay ring when possible; otherwise the server emits `event: reset` before continuing live. A
client that ignores `id:`/`reset` behaves exactly as before this was added.

parameters.name: last_event_id
parameters.description: Resume id from a previous `id:` (or `event: reset`) — for callers that cannot set headers. Ignored when the `Last-Event-ID` header is present.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Resume id from a previous `id:` (or `event: reset`); set automatically by a native `EventSource`'s auto-reconnect. Takes precedence over `?last_event_id=`.

200.description: SSE stream of key change events. Every event carries an `id:`. Event types: `set` / `delete` (data: the key) and `reset` (data: `{"reason": ...}`, emitted whenever gapless resume cannot be guaranteed — the client should re-read the domain, then keep applying events normally).

get.summary: Reads the last N lines of a log file (spec general/005).

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: Tail line count from file end (default 100, capped at 1000). 0 is rejected.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-sensitive substring filter; only matching lines count toward `lines`.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Name of a file listed by GET /logs/files. Defaults to the newest luradb.log* file.

200.description: Tail of the selected log file

500.description: log directory unreadable, no luradb.log* file found, or read failed

get.summary:
Lists every `luradb.log*` file in the log directory (spec general/005).
`files[0]` is exactly the file `GET /logs` reads without a `file` param.
`GET /metrics` — system + all domain metrics. Admin only.
get.description:
`engines` (spec general/019) is an additive block, one entry per storage
engine (`kv`/`json`/`rel`), each with the same nine fields: `read_ops`,
`write_ops`, `read_latency_us_p50/p95/p99`, `write_latency_us_p50/p95/p99`,
`window_secs`. Clients compute `read_ops / window_secs` for ops/s — the
rate is a `window_secs`-wide average, not an instantaneous value, since
`read_ops`/`write_ops` only count fully ticked seconds (the running
second is excluded). A disabled engine still gets its block, all zero —
`0` for a latency percentile means no op landed in the window, not an
unmeasurably fast one.

get.summary: `GET /metrics/domains/{name}` — metrics for one domain. Admin or domain user.

404.description: Domain not found or no metrics yet

get.summary: Returns all active relational domains.

post.summary:
Creates a new relational domain (isolated table/view namespace, separate
from KV and JSON domains).

get.summary:
Returns metadata for a single relational domain. A domain in `deleting`
state answers 410 Gone (rel/013 finishes the physical purge).

410.description: Domain is being deleted (background purge running)

delete.summary:
Marks a relational domain as deleting. Its tables/views become
inaccessible immediately; physical cleanup follows in rel/013.

post.summary:
Executes exactly one LuraSQL statement against `domain` and returns its
typed result. `expand` resolves REFERENCES columns of a SELECT into
embedded objects (or `"*"` for every REFERENCES column).

200.description: Statement result. Shape depends on the statement class — DDL: {"ok":true}; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE: {"affected","last_pk"}; SELECT: {"columns":[{"name","type"}],"rows":[[...]],"row_count","limit_applied","expanded"?}. `rows` are arrays (not objects) so same-named JOIN columns don't collide.

400.description: Syntax, type, parameter-count, or expand error

403.description: Access level too low for this statement (rel/011)

404.description: Domain, table, column, or index not found

409.description: Conflict — duplicate key, unique violation, name collision, …

get.summary: Lists the tables of a domain (views are listed separately, `GET …/views`).

Returns a table's schema (columns, indexes) plus HATEOAS links. A view
name answers 404 here — use `GET …/views` for views.

404.description: Domain or table not found (a view is not a table)

get.summary:
Counts the rows of `table` — the same residual-free access path `SELECT
COUNT(*) FROM table` would use via `/sql`, without a SQL round trip. A
view answers 404 here, same as `GET …/rows` (no row-level resource in v1).

200.description: Row count. A full key scan under the hood — cost grows linearly with table size; meant for on-demand use, not high-frequency polling.

404.description: Domain or table not found (a view has no count resource, same as `rows`)

get.summary:
Lists rows of `table`. Every query parameter other than `expand`/`limit`/
`offset` is an equality filter on the like-named column (`?col=value`,
AND-combined); parse errors and unknown filter columns answer 400. This
compiles onto the same bound `*`-SELECT plan `/sql` would use.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: Comma-separated REFERENCES columns to resolve, or "*" for all

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max rows to return (falls back to the configured default, capped at the configured max)

200.description: Matching rows as objects, with row_count/limit/offset/limit_applied

400.description: Unknown filter column, or a filter/limit/offset parse/type error

post.summary:
Inserts one row from a JSON object body (`{column: value, …}`). An omitted
AUTOINCREMENT primary key is assigned the next sequence value (rel/005
§9); this compiles onto the exact same bound INSERT plan `/sql` would use.

403.description: Missing read access to a linked KV/JSON domain (rel/016)

404.description: Domain, table, or referenced body column not found

409.description: PK collision, unique violation, or missing REFERENCES target

get.summary:
Fetches a single row by primary key — the same PK-point SELECT plan
`/sql`'s `WHERE pk = ?` would use.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: Comma-separated REFERENCES columns to resolve, or "*"

200.description: The row as an object, with an optional _expanded block

404.description: Domain, table, or row not found

put.summary:
Partially updates a row by primary key: only the columns named in the
body are set, everything else stays unchanged (spec §5). Not an upsert —
a PK the table doesn't have answers 404, never a create.

400.description: NOT NULL/type/schema violation, or body primary key != path primary key

403.description: Missing read access to a linked KV/JSON domain (rel/016)

404.description: Domain, table, column, or row not found

409.description: Unique violation, or missing REFERENCES target

delete.summary:
Deletes a row by primary key. Hanging REFERENCES from other tables are
not blocked by this (rel/005 §11) — they resolve to `null` afterwards.

404.description: Domain, table, or row not found

get.summary: Lists the views of a domain, including their raw (unmodified) SQL text.

200.description: Views of the domain, incl. raw SQL text

get.summary:
Live status of a restore job. Lives in RAM only (spec general/006) — gone
after a restart; the outcome is also in the log.
`GET /version` — version handshake. Requires any valid API key.

401.description: Unauthorized — a valid API key is required

BackupDetailResponse.description:
Manifest fields + state + size (spec general/006 GET /backups/{id} and
POST /backups/upload). Everything but `id`/`state`/`scope` is optional:
the currently-running-job shape (`running`) only fills `started_at`; the
complete/incomplete shape fills the rest instead.

key.description: Document key or "line N" for parse errors.

CountResponse.description:
Generic `{"count": N}` response, shared by JSON's `count_documents`, KV's
`count_keys`, and rel's `count_rows` (spec general/017) — one schema
instead of three identical ones.

include_auth.description: Only effective for `all`/`kv` scopes (auth records live in the KV instance).

scope.description:
`all` | `kv` | `json` | `kv:<domain>` | `json:<domain>` | `domain:<name>`.
Covers the KV and JSON engines only — relational data is never included.

field.description: JSON field path, dot notation for nested fields (e.g. "address.city").

api_key.description: API key (visible only once — cannot be retrieved afterward).

DocumentResponse.description:
A document as returned by the store: `_key`/`_version` metadata merged
into the user's fields.

_version.description: Write counter: 1 on create, incremented on every write.

additionalProperties.description:
The document's own fields. A document whose content is not a JSON
object appears as a single `_content` field holding that value.

document_count.description: Number of documents — only set on the detail endpoint.

expires_at.description: Absolute Unix-seconds TTL expiry; `null` when the key has no TTL. Equal to the `X-Expires-At` header when present.

last_modified_at.description: Unix-milliseconds write time of the newest visible version (PUT, or PATCH …/null) — not a creation timestamp; every overwrite advances it.

file.description: Name of a file listed by `GET /logs/files`. Defaults to the newest `luradb.log*` file.

lines.description: Tail line count from the file end (default 100, capped at 1000). `0` is rejected.

q.description: Case-sensitive substring filter; only matching lines count toward `lines`.

file.description: Name of the file actually read, without a path.

truncated.description: `true` iff the scan budget was exhausted before `lines` matches and before file start.

PermissionItem.description:
One entry of a user's domain permission matrix. `store_type`/`access` are
lowercase and match the write-endpoint vocabulary exactly (`parse_store_type`,
`access` parsing in `set_permission`) — usable as-is in a follow-up request.

field.description: Optional: re-index only this field's index. Omit for all indexes.

state.description:
Lifecycle state: "active" or "deleting" (background purge running, rel/013).
Always present — so rel/013's later `list_domains` visibility change
(surfacing `Deleting` domains too) needs no REST-contract change.

include_auth.description: Apply auth-user/auth-perm lines from the archive (upsert). Default false.

into_domain.description:
Only legal when the archive contains exactly one domain name
(`kv:*`/`json:*`/`domain:*` scopes).

api_key.description: New API key (visible only once — cannot be retrieved afterward).

rows.description:
One JSON object per row (catalog column order in principle; `serde_json`'s
default map is unordered/alphabetical here, see rel_browse.rs module docs),
with an optional `_expanded` block (spec §6).

store_type.description: Store type of the domain: `"kv"` (default), `"json"` (spec json/012) or `"rel"` (spec rel/011).

expand.description:
REFERENCES columns to resolve into embedded objects, or `["*"]` for
all of them (§5). Only valid for SELECT; non-empty on DML/DDL → 400.

params.description:
Positional parameters (JSON array), bound to the `?` placeholders
(rel/004/005). Omitted ⇒ empty array.

permissions.description: Domain permission matrix — see `list_users` doc for `role == "Admin"` semantics.

api_version.description: API contract version — identical to the contract's `info.version`.

WhoamiResponse.description:
Caller identity. `role` is the only discriminator between the four cases —
see `whoami` for the full mapping; `name` is `null` whenever no
`UserRecord` backs the caller (`TrustedPeer`, `Disabled`).

role.description:
`"Admin"`, `"User"`, or a pseudo-role: `"TrustedPeer"` (UDS peer
authenticated by the kernel, spec perf/001) or `"Disabled"`
(`auth.enabled = false`).

bearer_auth.description: API key as configured in `luradb.toml` (admins), or as received on user creation / key rotation. Only required when `auth.enabled = true`.

tags.name: Domains
tags.description: Domain lifecycle — create, list, get, delete

tags.name: Relational Browse
tags.description: Catalog and row browsing for relational domains

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: User management and domain permissions — admins only, except GET /auth/whoami (any authenticated caller)

tags.name: Logs
tags.description: Read-only log tail and file listing — admins only, opt-in via log.http_access

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Global lifecycle/DDL event stream (SSE) across the KV, JSON and relational engines — admins only
